searches.note: Twenty two searches of twenty eight, six unspent. Searches restricted to temata.co.nz, craggyrange.com and missionestate.co.nz are read as the house through their summaries; teara.govt.nz as the national encyclopedia. Some searches blocked the author's own sources (decanter.com, craggyrange.com, Wine Anorak, Wine With Seth) so the second source would be independent. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: founding, people and dates, grapes, sites, making, ageing, serving, label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail stood in one source or none it was cut or said with less.

Writers' own sites (Wine Anorak, Wine With Seth, Cameron Douglas, Raymond Chan, Jane Anson) met among the results are not cited in the fragment; the author's Wine Anorak and Wine With Seth sources were replaced.

tested: Bernard Chambers 1859 to 1931, born at Te Mata, sheep farmer: Te Ara biography. Sound.
Vines from 1892, Pinot Noir cuttings among the first: Te Ara and the house; the cuttings came from the Marist mission at Taradale. Sharpened.
First wine by 1895: Te Ara (March 1895); the house gives 1894 for its first official vintage and 1896 as its founding. Kept as Te Ara, 1896 as the founding (the library's year).
Largest producer by 1910: Te Ara's Wine entry (1910) and the house (1909). Sound.
Sale of 1917: Te Ara, October 1917, the winery, stocks and part of the vineyard, most of the station five months later; the house and Wikipedia say 1919. Changed to Te Ara's terms.
Revival of 1974: Te Ara and the house. Sound.

First Coleraine 1982, single vineyard until 1989, named for the vineyard and family home, itself named for the Northern Irish town an ancestor was born in: the house, Wilson Daniels, Hawke's Bay Today. Changed.
Oak: the house's own article gives 18 to 20 months with around 30 per cent new; a critic's summary predominantly new. Mostly new cut.
Decanter Wine Legend for the 1998 in 2017: the house's release (August 2017 issue) and Hawke's Bay Today; first or only New Zealand wine so named in both, told as the house's account. Sound, hedged.

tested: Founded 1998, an Australian family with a Master of Wine as partner: Decanter, Kobrand, Ratcliffe and the house's vineyard page (bought and first planted 1998). Sound; the region record's 1997 should read 1998.
First commercial vintage 2001 with Le Sol, Sophia and The Quarry: Decanter and a merchant. Sound.
Gimblett Gravels association of 2001, trademark, soil defined, the 1867 flood, a first for the New World as the association believes: the association, geotrips and others. Sound, hedged as written.

Making: the house's sheets of 2021 to 2024 give whole bunches from none to 65 per cent, indigenous and inoculated yeast by vintage, a French oak cuve and open steel, 24 to 28 days on skins, 17 months in French and Austrian barriques, demi-muids and puncheons, 32 to 45 per cent new. Changed.
Ageing: no source gave the house's fifteen years. Changed.

tested: Pakowhai 1851, Meeanee 1858: Te Ara and the Cyclopedia of New Zealand (Meeanee founded 1858). Sound.

The move to Greenmeadows: the house says its main house was cut into eleven sections in late 1910 and hauled nearly five kilometres by traction engine; Te Ara says the seminary moved in 1911. Changed: the record had the seminary sawn into eleven pieces in 1911.
The cottage carried to Meeanee in 1858: in no source read. Cut.

A French brother trained in the Loire selling wine beyond the mission: not found; the house says Brother Cyprien Huchet arrived at Meeanee in 1871 and extended the vineyards. Changed, his dates not found, so described.
Jewelstone Syrah from Mere Road, about 12 months in French oak, 23 to 30 per cent new: the house's sheets and a critic's summary. Changed to a quarter to a third.
Huchet as the house's top range made only in exceptional years: the house's Huchet pages. Sound.

tested: Founded 1897 by a settler from Luxembourg: Hawke's Bay Today (120th year in 2017) and the author's merchant account. Sound.

Tom McDonald 1907 to 1987, born at Greenmeadows, in the cellar from 1921, bought the business in 1927 at nineteen by his own account: Te Ara; one Herald account has the founder dying in 1936 and the purchase after. Changed: the founder's return to Europe and the lease cut, the 1927 hedged as his account.
Sold to Ballins Breweries in 1944, McDonald staying as manager; the new winery of 1948: Te Ara. Added.
The 1949 Cabernet Sauvignon told as among the first commercial wines of the grape: Wikipedia and the Herald. Sound as hedged.
Merged with McWilliam's in 1962, McDonald production director: Te Ara and a winery history. Sound, sharpened.
Montana in 1988 or 1989, the Church Road brand of 1989 to 1990, Allied Domecq 2001, Pernod Ricard 2005: Te Ara, Wikipedia, the Herald. Sound.
TOM first of 1995, unveiled in 1999 with the Tom McDonald Cellar, only in exceptional years: the Waikato Times, the house's note quoted by a merchant. Sound.
Blend: Cabernet predominant in the mid 1990s, Merlot important from 1998, the 2007 at 51 to 49, the 2018 at 85 to 15: changed.
Barrel time 15 to 27 months across the notes; malolactic in barrique: changed.
TOM Chardonnay and TOM Syrah (from 2013) beside the red, only in exceptional years: the Listener and the press. Sound; the McDonald Series' launch of 2012 not found, cut.

swaps.proposed: wine: Jewelstone Syrah to Huchet Syrah
swaps.why: The house does call Huchet its highest range, made only in exceptional years, but the record is written whole for Jewelstone and says plainly where it stands; Huchet's first vintage, its making and its sites were not found in this run, so a rewrite could not be refuted here. Jewelstone Syrah is the single vineyard wine of the house most reviewed and met. The integrator may revisit with a rewritten and refuted record.

codexTension: The region record's producers line gives Craggy Range as founded in 1997; the library, the house and Decanter give 1998.
The library's wine note calls Coleraine New Zealand's most collected red: a ranking the flagships record does not repeat; Decanter's own words are the most avidly collected.
The library's note that Coleraine is made only in the better years was not confirmed (author's report, unchanged).
The region summary calls Mission Estate the country's oldest winery; the house says first winery and Te Ara oldest surviving winemaker: consistent, but a claim of a first.
